messages:
sam_support: FYI customer (AtlasPay) escalated — after yesterday's model swap to opus-3a we're seeing a spike in parsing failures for structured_output (JSON). They hit it in prod, app-side JSON.parse blows up.

ronan_oncall: Can you paste one example response they got? also which model variant exactly (quant / fp16)?

sam_support: Pasting sanitized snippet from their logs: 
```
response: '{\"amount\": 100, \"currency\": "USD",, \"metadata\": "notes: confirmed
reference: abc123"}'
error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 19 (char 18)
```
They say it started ~10:02 UTC right after we pointed traffic at opus-3a-standard (fp16).

maria_sre: Checking telemetry — overall 400s from customers processing layer up ~+3.2% since 10:00, structured_output 500s/internal also +1.1%. Dropped latency is fine, token rate steady.

li_prod: This looks like bad escaping + stray comma. Could be model emitting literal newlines or unescaped colons inside string fields. Did we change the response_format or prompt template during rollout?

sam_support: No prompt changes. Only model swap in routing policy. Customer uses our JSON mode with response_format set to {type: json, schema: invoice}.

ronan_oncall: Repro steps I used locally (curl):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"opus-3a-standard","input":"extract invoice as json", "structured_output":true}'
```
I get occasional outputs with: unescaped newlines in values, trailing commas, and double commas between fields. Repro rate ~12% on a short loop with our sample prompt.

deploy-bot: rollout opus-3a-standard -> traffic 100% at 2026-02-25T09:58:20Z

maria_sre: I ramped down opus-3a to 0% for the affected customers at 10:18 UTC and re-routed them back to opus-2c. Metrics recovering, parsing error rate dropping back toward baseline (~10:25 UTC).

li_prod: Thanks — that strongly implies model behavioral drift (schema hallucination). Short-term mitigation: pin customers to opus-2c or add a post-processing strict JSON sanitizer as a fallback. Long term: train a response_format enforcement wrapper in the serving runtime.

ronan_oncall: Filed incident tracker: INC-2026-319 with repro logs and a binary diff of example outputs. Also captured raw token stream from a failing request: 
```
... 0x22 0x61 0x6d 0x6f 0x75 0x6e 0x74 0x22 0x3a 0x20 0x31 0x30 0x30 0x2c 0x2c 0x20 0x22 0x63 0x75 0x72 0x72 0x65 0x6e 0x63 0x79 ...
```
(This shows the extra 0x2c comma byte)

sam_support: Customer confirmed that rollback fixed their failing processing flows. They're happy for now but requested a postmortem and a guarantee this won't repeat for other tenants.

li_prod: Action items: 1) Add stricter response_format enforcement in the pre-send validator (short-term PR). 2) Add model-level gating tests in the onboarding pipeline for structured_output before routing. 3) Investigate whether opus-3a tokenizer/decoding changes cause unescaped control chars.

maria_sre: I'm assigning myself on the rollback/playbook updates and will add an automatic mitigation rule: if structured_output parse errors >0.5% for a tenant within 15m, auto-route that tenant to last-stable model.

ronan_oncall: Quick mitigation PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/serve/pulls/789 — server-side sanitizer that attempts safe-json repair + logs a reject reason. Not perfect but reduces customer-visible 400s.

sam_support: I'll schedule a follow-up with the customer to confirm the mitigation and scope their tolerance for future model swaps.

li_prod: Next steps for ML team: run a batch of schema-specific samplers against opus-3a with strict output constraints, record token-level diffs vs opus-2c, and update model profile. I'll open ML task TKT-412.

maria_sre: Noting for ops: don't promote new model variants to 100% until they pass structured_output smoke tests for our top 10 schemas.

sam_support: Closing loop here for the channel — customer unblocked after rollback, we've got a mitigation PR and triage items. Will post postmortem once ML analysis and ops playbook updates are done. :white_check_mark:
